reviews.text: Thank you for the great rating, diego salgado! We're here to provide the best quality care and expertise, and are glad to see we succeeded. Our team appreciates you taking the time to leave us a review!
Very rude . They hung up on me and didn’t address my issue.

The reception staff, the nurse, and especially the veterinarian were all kind.
I visited as a walk-in on a Sunday. I appreciated that they didn't pressure me into getting unnecessary tests.
Also, I had suspected an intestinal obstruction, but it turned out to be the ingestion of a chemical substance.
My pet hadn't been able to eat anything and was just vomiting for three days, but recovered after the visit to the clinic.
I spent nearly $900 on X-rays, blood tests, and medication. It was expensive, but I know other places charge similar rates.
Thank you for the wonderful rating! We certainly appreciate your trust. We're here to deliver quality veterinary care whenever you need us.
Affordable and nice employees

We had an incredible experience at Echo Park Veterinary Hospital, especially with Holly Polk. We came in needing urgent care for our 16.5-year-old dog, and not only were we seen and treated the same day, but the entire team showed genuine care for our boy throughout.

Holly Polk was thorough, patient, and kind — she has this great balance of being matter-of-fact while staying calm and reassuring, which made a stressful situation so much easier.

Since then, we’ve had to come back a couple of times for a persistent ear infection, and every time the staff has been accommodating about getting us in quickly. Dr. Przekop saw us on one of these return visits and was great as well. Everyone we’ve dealt with has been friendly and communicative. Overall, we’ve had a wonderful experience with the care our dog has received here, and we’re grateful to have found them.

Hi Em, thank you for taking the time to leave us a rating. We pride ourselves on providing the best care, and we're disappointed you did not have a great experience with us. We'd love to know where we fell short. Please contact us at (323) 663-1107 if you have any additional feedback. We hope, if ever needed, you trust us to take care of you and your pet.

It felt like just a boring transaction. 3 out of 5 staff members were not hospitable, just “ doing their job” attitude. I even tried a couple times to start a conversation but on the bright side, pricing is very transparent and they don’t upsell. So meh

I took my cat there because he had an injury on his leg and couldn't walk, and I could tell he was in immense pain. They couldn't tell what was wrong with him, even after X-rays. After $600 They said just take him home and if it gets worse, bring him back. Well, after 2 weeks, he started limping again, and I noticed a large growth on his leg. I looked at the X-rays and noticed that they DID NOT xray that part of his leg where the growth was forming. I took him back and showed them that they were negligent in their examination, and NOT ONE  of the staff would apologize, let alone admit they did anything wrong. The doctor who examined my cat originally was not there, and everyone just kept making excuses for him, saying that he just didn't x-ray that part of his leg because he didn't think it was necessary. What?? My cat has never fully recovered. He can't even jump up on the bed easily. I can't say whether it would've been different if the injury had been found in the original examination, but it may have helped to treat him sooner. They were all so unapologetic and indifferent. And to top it off, when I brought him back, they charged me for the second set of X-rays that had to be done because the first ones that I paid for were botched inproperly done. Another $250!! I will never go here again,
Thank you for the wonderful rating! We take a lot of pride in delivering the best care and are glad you had a great experience with us.

Thank you for the great rating, Francine Jenzen! We're here to provide the best quality care and expertise, and are glad to see we succeeded. Our team appreciates you taking the time to leave us a review!

I brought my foster kitten Nutter Butter here on a Sunday morning after he got some nasty conjunctivitis Saturday. The poor little guy was very uncomfortable, and I am so grateful Echo Park Veterinary Hospital was able to accept us as walk-ins.

We waited for a little over an hour, and the time passed quickly thanks to all the other lovely pet guardians in the lobby. Treatment was thorough, efficient, and reasonably priced. I even walked out with flea meds for NB and his two siblings at home.

Thank you for all you do for our sweet critters!

First time today after changing vet and the visit with my cat who has an infected eye was great ! Doctor was very kind and knowledgeable, willing to explain medication also the ones I already have at home and we left happy to have found our new vet ! Thank you ! They weren’t secretive about costs and procedures and price was totally acceptable! Sheeba says thank you !
I take my cat into this vet & they are incredibly kind & knowledgeable! A checkup only cost me $25 which feels very fair. I highly recommend brining ur pets here (:

Booked an appointment the day before over the phone and showed up the next morning to no one there and no one answering the phone. There were other people showing up for their appointments and they didn’t notify anyone they weren’t open. Apparently it was a staffing issue but to not alert anyone, after confirming the day before, is extremely unprofessional.
i will always recommend echo park vet! every time i go, they don’t disappoint with their efficiency & care for my dog! i always regret not going here first especially during an emergency.
My dog is sick
“Have been bringing my pets here since 2016, and I truly trust this team. The doctors are honest, compassionate, and always go the extra mile to make sure every animal is cared for like family.”

The vet was so kind and doesn’t try to up sell you. Genuinely cares about your dogs well being. Pretty affordable compared to most vets, we just walked in as we were able to get seen in a timely manner
Excellent service for our precious animals and reasonable prices. Highly recommended.
Staff super nice and caring and clean

Echo Park Veterinary hospital are the BEST. Switched to Mohawk on Sunset and was THAT a MISTAKE! Dr David and his Staff are the BEST! No comment related to Mohawk other than THEY dropped the ball on the health care they provided for my senior cat that almost cost him his life! Veterinary Hospital is avaliable no matter the circumstance! ER issue with your loved one at Mohawk... horific experience denied help when you need it!

The lady doctor is very professional. She is incredibly humble. She loves her job and loves animals. I took my dog for issues with his jaws. He was in pain everytime he tried to open his mouth to eat. With few looks and touches She diagnosed the condition. No issues with the jaw. No issues with teeth. No infection. Just pain random. associated with age. Pain killer, hydration injections, anti itch shot. Few days.. and the dogs is as good as new. 😀 thank you mostly for the reassurance that all was going to be ok. And it has been. I recommend echo park vet. Easy to make appointments.  And they accept walk ins. ( not all vets locations have that feature. Very useful when. Yiu are worried about your pets health . Lol.) Reasonable price. Same day appointments. And they are busy. So thats a great feature.

The staff at Echo Park Veterinary Hospital are very professional and clearly have the welfare of our dogs in the forefront.  We feel very confident that our dogs will receive excellent care at Echo Park Vet.

they are thorough and lovely to work with. I brought a stray cat in and they did her exam and gave her her first vaccinations. I had called another animal hospital that said they couldn't and another one that couldn't see her that day so it was a relief when they were so present for her
Thank you for the wonderful rating! We take a lot of pride in delivering the best care and are glad you had a great experience with us.

This place is convenient, efficient, transparent and accommodating. There is parking in the back and they take walk ins during the day. Whether your matter is small or big the staff will take the time to make sure you understand what is needed and you understand the cost associated with it. Big shout out to Peter for being super helpful today!

My 18, year old female cat Princess , had been going to this hospital for a couple of years now, she had been a very healthy cat but like humans as you get older you develop illnesses. She was diagnosed with Hyperthyroidism, 3 months ago and was treated . This is a manageable long term illness,  but things go complicated . Her Thyroid medication gave her anemia and Dr Polk suspended the medication immediately. She progressively got worse. They then ran more tests and diagnosed her with pancreatitis, the steroids and treatments got her worse. I knew it was time to let her go , but I held on to some hope. I wanted to have her for the Holidays, but my worry was having to make that difficult decision to put her down. She gave me a last gift. She died at home on Christmas Day when I got home from work. I notified the hospital a couple of days after her passing and not even an email or call from her Dr to at least send their condolences.  I’m very disappointed with  customer relations. To me that’s not acting in a professional way. But to charge for treatments that don’t work and upcharge the bill, there they have no mercy. Money comes first and your pet come second. I read all those negative reviews and gave them the benefit of the doubt, but I made a bad decision taking my girl there. As a pet Dad I did all that was possible and I am at peace and I can go to bed with a clean conscience. Think twice before taking your most precious 4 legged family member there.☹️

A healthy 2.5 year-old dog shouldn’t walk into a clinic for a simple broken nail and leave his family searching for answers. I knew San well, and he was not only incredibly sweet and friendly, but full of energy and life. When I learned what happened, I was heartbroken. I genuinely can’t understand how this could happen under competent care.

What’s most concerning is the lack of accountability from Echo Park Veterinary Hospital. The explanation given to his family didn’t match the documentation, which appeared altered after the fact rather than recorded as events happened. Instead of a straightforward medical record, what they provided looked incomplete, contradictory, and edited only after San was already gone. When a perfectly healthy dog dies during a minor procedure and the paperwork raises more questions than answers, it becomes impossible not to view the care here as careless and incompetent.

Families shouldn’t have to fight for clarity after something this preventable. If a clinic stands behind its work, it should be able to explain it without vague language, altered notes, or avoidance of responsibility. If something like this ever happens to your pet, request every document and report discrepancies to the state veterinary board. Honest veterinarians should welcome oversight. Our animals deserve competent care, and families deserve accountability.

Echo Park Veterinary Hospital is by far the best vet we have used in the area. Their fees are reasonable and their care is always professional and compassionate.
Unlike so many other Vets in LA they do not upsell by stoking fear about the animals by adding unnecessary procedures and distressing speculations about the pets they care for. Instead the Doctors and staff provide straightforward diagnoses with treatment options. For example their charge for a minor surgery was exactly half of what other places had offered.
We love this vet! They really take their time and don’t rush. Dr Przekop is great.

ALL the staff here is so incredibly helpful, patient, and supportive. I went to another animal hospital in the neighborhood before coming here, and they treated my dog like he was a lost cause.

When I tried this animal hospital, they were very understanding of my pup and his behavioral issues. They made my pup feel safe and made us feel secure with the care they provided.

Dora has been coming here for years, and even though she’s a feisty 13 lb senior pup at the vet, the staff is always patient and calm with her. The front desk is super kind, both in person and when I call as the paranoid pet mom I am. Techs and doctors are great, and the relief vet we saw yesterday was amazing and answered all my questions. Pricing has always been clear and explained. Overall, nothing but good vibes and great care for my girl.
Never come to this place, because you will never see your baby again. My family dog died at Echo Park Veterinary Hospital. It's a disgusting and filthy place.

My extremely healthy 2.5 year old dog San died at Echo Park Veterinary Hospital while under anesthesia for a simple broken nail.

San was a super healthy pup, we would always take him on walks and to parks. He was full of life, usually the fastest dog in the park, running circles around other dogs. He had been under anesthesia before for his neuter and teeth cleaning and was always perfectly fine.

On 10/26, he broke his dewclaw at the park. It was a minor injury, there was barely any bleeding. My regular vet couldn't get us in, so I made the mistake of going to Echo Park Veterinary Hospital for the first time.

My appointment was at 2:30 pm, right after their lunch break, and my first impression was that the vet appeared sleepy. The vet listened to San's heart and said he sounded "strong” and gave me the treatment plan. When I saw it, I repeatedly asked if anesthesia was necessary for a simple nail trim. The technician insisted it was. It is clear in hindsight that they just wanted to upcharge me for a simple procedure. They took him away, and that was the last time I ever saw San alive.

A while later, the vet came out and told me San was dead. The vet told me it was likely a "pulmonary embolism." This was a complete lie. They let me into the "operating room," and I was horrified. The place looked run-down, and San was on a ventilator, but there wasn't even a heart monitor in sight.

Later, I was given the medical notes, all written after the event with parts scratched out. The notes indicate they tried to give him two 0.5cc of dexmedetomidine and claimed one "missed”. Most importantly, the notes show no attempt to administer Antisedan, the reversal agent for dexmedetomidine.

My perfectly healthy dog died on their table from a broken nail. I am sharing our story so this doesn't happen to anyone else's family. Do not take your pet to this hospital.

Hi Jayne, thank you for taking the time to leave us a rating. We pride ourselves on providing the best care, and we're disappointed you did not have a great experience with us. We'd love to know where we fell short. Please contact us at (323) 663-1107 if you have any additional feedback. We hope, if ever needed, you trust us to take care of you and your pet.

Hi Soo Ji Lee, thank you for leaving us a rating. We're disappointed to see we weren't able to provide you with a better experience. If you have additional feedback or concerns, feel free to contact us at (323) 663-1107. We hope that, if ever needed, you will visit us again for a better experience.

My brother’s healthy pup was killed here. Do not come here. This is a clinic with no accountability and pushes unnecessary medical procedures.

My brother’s 2.5 year old dog, San, was extremely active, healthy, and energetic, with no significant past medical history. He was strong and smart, always looking for ways to be in the outdoors. I was with San for an entire summer, where he was always running around my community park and backyard, and being social with other dogs, tiring me out as I played fetch with him for hours.

Due to this activity, he broke his dewclaw at the park. Seeing that this was a minor injury, my brother took him to a nearby vet instead of his usual provider for a broken nail. For incomprehensible, greedy financial reasons, the staff insisted to put San under GENERAL anesthesia. He never bites anyone, and was most likely scared by this cold, foreign environment.

San was then killed in the OR. No tests were performed to identify the cause of death, and the vet simply suggested that an underlying pulmonary embolism was the likely cause. The notes are written hastily, saying that the staff missed the first dose of anesthesia. No times were written down, and no monitoring was suggested in the notes despite the staff literally saying that they “missed” the first dose.

My brother and his wife are devastated. San’s death was completely preventable, and only caused by medical negligence and staff inattention. I will never be able to play fetch with San at the park, due to a freak operation for a nail trim. Please reconsider if you need veterinary care for your pet.

!!PLEAAASE!!don’t go to Echo Park Veterinary

My friend’s healthy 2-year-old dog passed away there after a simple broken nail treatment. The hospital said they needed to use general anesthesia, but later it turned out they didn’t even do a blood test beforehand. The medical record we received had signs of the drug dosage being altered.

What worse is, after the dog was given to the family the staff was laughing while the family was crying with a broken heart

No family should ever have to go through this kind of tragedy.

THEY KILLED MY FRIEND'S DOG

Please be cautious before bringing your pet here. My friend took her perfectly healthy dog in for what should've been a simple nail trim after it broke at the dog park. The vet suggested putting him under anesthesia -which felt extreme for such a minor procedure. Tragically, his heart stopped during the process and he didn't make it.

This wasn't their regular vet - it was a Sunday, so they went to a clinic that was open. But what makes this so devastating is that this could have been avoided.

Many vets, unfortunately, will recommend unnecessary procedures or medications to make more money, and anesthesia for a nail trim is beyond excessive. I've personally had my own dog undergo light sedation before for a similar issue and that is very different from full anesthesia.

To make matters worse, the way the staff handled the situation afterward was cold and unprofessional. The notes from his chart were inconsistent -- and when my friend and her husband were in tears over their dog's death, the front desk staff were joking around and laughing. There was no empathy, no accountability.

Losing a pet is heartbreaking enough, but to lose them because of negligence and carelessness is unforgivable. Please research where you take your pets carefully. No family should have to go through something like this over a nail trim.

Please be very cautious before bringing your pet to Echo Park Veterinary Hospital. My friend’s healthy 2 year old dog died here after a simple broken nail trim. Since it was Sunday, their regular vet was closed, so they came here for the first time. The vet insisted on full anesthesia, clearly to upcharge, and didn’t even do bloodwork before sedating him. The procedural plan notes were unclear, with scribbles over medication amounts, and the staff was cold and unempathetic, even laughing while my friends were grieving. It’s heartbreaking, and I sincerely hope no other pet parent experiences such pain. Please be careful where you take your family.

My sweet 2-year-old dog never returned home after he left to fix his broken nail. Please read my review before visiting this vet. Let our dog's death not be in vain. Instead, let it serve to save other lives.

I still can’t believe this at all. When I got a call from my husband that our dog had just passed away while trimming his broken nail, I immediately ran to the hospital with my 10-month-old baby. We saw our poor dog laying without any movement in such a cold room.

This was such a simple procedure. They could have literally asked my husband to hold him and fix the nail. Anesthesia was NEVER needed in the first place. Obviously, they tried to scam and overcharge us, which eventually resulted in my poor dog dying.

I had never thought this could ever happen to me. He was happily running and chasing other dogs in the dog park just 2 hours before he passed away. I am still in tears ever since Sunday, wishing I had one more day to cuddle him and take a long walk with him. If he were old or had a chronic condition, I would have prepared for his goodbye. But my poor boy was only 2 years old. Too young to die, too sudden. Now he is no longer with us. We are so devastated that he just disappeared in a blink.

Horrible clinic - if you want your pet to stay alive - do not come here! My friend dropped off his dog for a broken Duclaw and this clinic performed a full anesthesia and the dog never woke up.

According to their report, the dog was aggressive in the treatment room. Instead of calling the owner in, they suggested to pursue a full sedation for the treatment of a broken nail basically. The owner did agree to that after confirming multiple times that it was absolutely necessary. It is important to note that this dog is extremely sweet and kind and if he was "aggressive" he was probably just really scared.

The clinic then went on to sedate him WITHOUT doing any bloodwork. The vet could have easily done a PT INR test before any surgery to make sure the dog is fit, especially since this dog is not a usual patient there but was a drop-in.

My friend was then told he died of a pulmonary embolism - how would they have identified that? It is unclear how that would have been the cause especially as it is usually identified via Imaging (x-Ray e.g.) or Blood tests.

There are also no timestamps on the notes, it is unclear if a vet was even present when all of this happened and were the anesthesia drugs properly calculated based on his weight? I also wonder if the risks of this procedure were properly explained.

It leaves my friend without a beautiful dog he rescued - if you have a heart for animals do not consider this clinic.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
I had a fantastic experience at Echo Park Veterinary Office! They were able to take us in without an appointment, which was a huge relief. The staff was incredibly welcoming and professional, making sure that my dog, Leo, felt comfortable throughout his visit. He didn’t even seem nervous during the examination, which speaks volumes about the care they provide. I’m definitely planning to bring my cat in soon! Highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a caring veterinarian team.
Great people, great Dr.

I’ve been bringing my dog here for over a year and the service has been consistently excellent. The staff is knowledgeable, always answers my questions, and keeps thorough records of my dog’s vaccines. I also appreciate the helpful text reminders when he’s due for exams and vaccinations. Their app is another great feature, it even provides a digital pet ID that can be printed if needed. Highly recommend!
Very efficient and professional. I especially liked the cordial attitude of both the Vet and his assistant.
Great experience. Reasonable prices. Doctor was excellent. Get there before they open as there will be a line to get in to see doc.

Thanks for the rating! We're here to provide the best quality care and expertise. If ever needed, we hope we can provide an even better experience on your next visit. We appreciate you taking the time to leave us a review!

Great practice, the vets, vet assistants and other staff are all patient, kind, and helpful. While not super cheap, costs are reasonable.  I like their service model (walk-in in the morning, drop in for pickup in the late afternoon), less stressful and more efficient than scheduled appointments. The only downside (which is out of the control of the practice) is that parking on the one street available to park on has become  more difficult ever since a yoga studio moved in next door.

My cat had to be NARCAN-ed twice after a visit here for a toenail issue. Without my knowledge or consent he was given a transdermal 4-day-lasting opiate approved only for post-surgery usage, which was also contraindicated to his kidney disease (they didn't ask about his medical history at all). Upon arriving home, he turned into a zombie: couldn't blink, couldn't sleep, couldn't eat, couldn't drink, couldn't pee, couldn't poop. It took two doses of Narcan at my regular vet over the next two days to save his life.
As others have mentioned, this place is filthy and the exam rooms are full of the pet hair of previous patients. I came here because my usual vet didn't have an opening and it didn't seem serious enough for LAASER, but had a terrible feeling as soon as I walked in and saw how dirty it was. Little did I know they'd be so negligent as to mistreat my cat to the point where he would have died without immediate intervention elsewhere. Take your pet anywhere else.

My dog Minnie has never liked going to the vet—but Echo Park Veterinary Hospital has changed everything. We’ve been there many times, and every visit they treat her with such gentle love and patience. Even when she’s scared, they understand her. They never rush. They always care. It means everything to me to see her treated like family. I truly trust them with her life. This place is a blessing
I waited 4 hours for them to charge twice as much as other nearby vets. Nelson was very impolite. Definitely try elsewhere!!
I did a walk-in  the told that sorry but u need a appointment .my dog was really sick they didn't care
I took my pitbull to him always came through for me no regrets would highly recommend him.....
Thank you for the great rating! We're here to provide the best quality care and expertise, and are glad to see we succeeded. Our team appreciates you taking the time to leave us a review!

I took my dog here because my primary vet was fully booked. My dog has a slipped disc and after doing some xrays, said he didn't need surgery. Then sent me home with some medication. Well he had complete paralysis of his rear legs so I took him to my primary vet two days later and they said I had to get him to ER immediately. The ER doctor said with slipped discs, time is of the essence. Thankfully I got him in for surgery a few days after his first symptoms so they said the chance of him walking again his pretty high with PT. If I didn't get the 2nd opinion from my primary vet, he could have been crippled for the rest of his life or worse.

This place is great! Great veterinarian, great service, thoughtful, courteous. Great and reasonable prices. They take very good care of my dog. Good parking.
We have been coming here for over 20 years and we highly recommend it for all your pet needs..

Very fast, they checked my dog out, they diagnosed her, sent her home with meds, right after she was feeling 10x better. They put a fluid bubble on her back! Gave her a shot! She is at home making a great recovery, it’s almost like she didn’t get sick! It was also very affordable!

I really like echo Park veterinarian hospital they're caring and affordable. At other veterinarians I have to drag my dog in, but at echo Park veterinarian hospital my dog walks in before I do. That's a plus in itself

Very disappointed with the level of care this place provides. A miscommunication between staff lead to me being misinformed about what I would be charged for. The examination rooms are visibly dirty which raises concerns about their overall hygiene standards. What shocked me most was the apparent lack of professionalism; hearing someone on the doctors side scrolling through reels on their phone while I was in the examination room did not instill confidence that my pet’s health was their top priority. While I understand that no vet can make antibiotics work or guarantee recovery, I expected a higher level of empathy and understanding, especially since we’ve been dealing with my cat’s condition for over six months. I simply do not recommend this place.
Thank you for the wonderful rating! We take a lot of pride in delivering the best care and are glad you had a great experience with us.

Very good experience, very nice people and a very clean clinic! I had to take my cousin’s cat in on an emergency. I was seeing quickly, and the issue was dealt with professionally, and the prices were fantastic! I am seriously, considering having my own animals records transferred here. So happy I found these guys.
Great service , nice staff, my dog had a surgery and ever since he is doing great considering he is a senior. Thank you Doctor!

I’m so grateful for the team at Echo Park Veterinary. I brought my French Bulldog in after two weeks of her not feeling well. We had already seen an emergency pet hospital, where they ran tests and told us it might be the early signs of IVDD. That was really scary to hear. We followed up with a regular vet who thought it might be a knee issue and told us to go to a bigger hospital if things didn’t get better.
She wasn’t improving, so I brought her to Echo Park Vet—and I’m so glad I did. The vet there did a very detailed exam and quickly noticed things no one else had: a slight head tilt, balance issues, and sure enough, when she checked her ears, she found infections in both. They gave her a steroid shot, cleaned her ears, and sent us home with antibiotics and ear drops.
It’s only been three days, but the difference is already clear—she’s moving better, her energy is coming back, and she looks more like herself. I truly believe she was misdiagnosed before, and Echo Park Vet finally got to the root of the issue.
On top of that, the cost of the visit and medication was surprisingly reasonable. I left feeling taken care of, not taken advantage of. I highly recommend this clinic—they genuinely care and pay attention.

I wouldn’t recommend this place to my worst enemy. I had such a traumatic experience that it’s taken me one year to post the review. I took my cat that had heart disease for his check up. When he came back from the X rays he could barely breathe. I let the tech and Dr Prescott know and they put him on temporary oxygen and gave him an additional injection. I took him home and he died within minutes. I was still charged $600 for them essentially killing my cat. When I called the office , there was no accountability or compassion. I will never set foot in that place again and I recommend not to trust Dr. Prescott as he was busy talking about music to my husband while my cat was having a medical crisis.
They turned us away when our cat urgently needed care because the entire staff was on break.
Franklin had urinary track issue, he still alive to this day. I recommend everyone to take their pets here. I want to thank everyone from the front desk to the techs and doctors. Thank you.

I've debated writing this, but after what happened to my puppy, and reading how many others have gone through similar or worse, I feel a responsibility to speak up. Veterinarians like Dr. Holly Polk are actively harming animal welfare through willful negligence and outdated, reckless care.

I brought my 9-week-old Miniature Schnauzer puppy to Echo Park Vet in February. She weighed just 2 lbs, was visibly underweight, and tested positive for Giardia and Cystoisospora, two intestinal parasites. They took her to the back, then told me she'd been given the first half of a deworming pill and I should administer the second half at home. Weeks later, when I went to give it, I realized the pill was completely intact. She had received no treatment at all. She could have died.

Additionally, the clinic completely failed to identify or act on clear signs of malnutrition and illness, including a bloated abdomen (commonly associated with parasites or protein deficiency), extremely low weight for her age and breed (2 lbs at 9 weeks for a Miniature Schnauzer), visible ribs and bony spine, weak muscle tone, low energy, a dry, patchy coat, and a small, stunted body frame. These are textbook red flags for undernourishment, especially in a parasite-positive puppy, and yet Echo Park Vet made no mention of concern, no follow-up plan, and listed her as medically "healthy."

The socialization advice I received was equally dangerous. I was told to treat her like an "unvaccinated newborn" and not expose her to new spaces until 16 weeks, advice that directly contradicts every current veterinary behavioral guideline. The critical socialization window is 8-16 weeks. Missing that window can lead to long-term behavioral issues, which are a leading cause of shelter surrender and euthanasia, especially in Los Angeles. Dr. Polk's guidance was dangerously out of step with modern veterinary standards. It was medically reckless and shows a clear disregard for staying informed.

Weeks later, I requested a temporary spay exemption so I could license my puppy in LA, which legally requires either proof of spay or a vet-signed exemption for intact dogs. I provided her rabies certificate, a full medical summary from her primary vet in Connecticut recommending delayed spay, and the county's official exemption form. Dr. Polk refused to sign, stating there was "no contrary indication for spaying." She declined to re-evaluate my puppy, speak with me directly, or acknowledge the very real health risks of spaying a small, still-developing dog at 19 weeks. This was not a refusal based on medical assessment, it was a blanket denial, and in my opinion, medical negligence.

I am filing a formal complaint with the California Veterinary Medical Board and am in touch with others who've experienced similar harm or dismissal at this clinic.

Echo Park Vet is not the clinic it used to be. If you have a small breed dog, a young puppy, or need informed, individualized care, please be careful. What happened to us is not just inconvenient: it's shameful, lazy, and dangerous.

update: 1 year later and dropping from 3 to 1 star… brought our dog in for urgent treatment, they first wanted to charge us 600… and dropped it down to ~250 since there were unnecessary charges before any check was done. Of course, same as before, they don’t know what is causing the issue, no recommendations, just wait to see if bleeding stops. They sent us home with prescriptions that are more for prevention than treatment. Very disappointing and never coming back again.

2023:
pretty good place that takes walk-ins only, prices for shots & regular check ups are pretty reasonable.. I’m not sure if I’d recommend for anything more. I took my cat for a check up since she was throwing up several times during a period of time then 5-6 times within a day span. They took her x-rays and when going over them, the vet was unsure of the results..
